Live `openral deploy sim` graph (slam + nav2 + octomap, reasoner on, no policy dispatched) on q-laptop / RTX 5070 Laptop, ROS 2 Jazzy, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp. One graph launch per scene, each at its pinned seed. Nav2 driven by a single direct NavigateToPose goal 2.0 m ahead in `map`, so the base translates and both rolling windows sweep new geometry. Produced by `tools/_nav2_costmap_silhouette_probe.py`: every cell centre of every published Costmap is transformed into base_link and tested against the manifest's bare chassis polygon (`base_footprint_polygon`) plus any attached primitives, using `payload_scan_filter_node`'s own containment predicates. Re-run 2026-09-05 after code review tightened the tool: `verdict` and the exit code now honour the non-vacuity guards, so a costmap that marked nothing anywhere reports VACUOUS instead of clean. `total_marked_in_silhouette` counts cells at exactly LETHAL_OBSTACLE (254) - not 253, which is what an inflation layer writes near a legitimate obstacle somewhere else.

finding: The GLOBAL costmap is EMPTY on both scenes: max cost 0 over 50 and 52 published samples, zero non-zero cells at any point, while the LOCAL costmap on the same graph peaks at 254 with 1982 / 1050 non-zero cells. Its `obstacle_layer` is configured on the same filtered `/openral/nav2/scan` the local costmap's `voxel_layer` reads, `static_layer` is deliberately out of its plugin chain (rolling window, SLAM-from-scratch), and `planner_server` logs no warning of any kind. NavfnPlanner therefore planned the accepted NavigateToPose goal against a blank 20x20 m grid. Not what #192 set out to measure, not fixed here, and it makes the GLOBAL half of the silhouette verdict VACUOUS - nothing is marked inside the robot because nothing is marked at all. The LOCAL half is non-vacuous and is the result this file records.

root_cause: The global costmap's emptiness is the HEIGHT FILTER, not the topic and not TF. Measured on a live graph: global_costmap IS subscribed to /openral/nav2/scan with matching BEST_EFFORT QoS (3 subscribers: local_costmap, collision_monitor, global_costmap), and 97 of 102 scans transform into `map` at their own stamps (map<-odom is 0.35-0.50 s AHEAD of each scan stamp; /tf runs at 62 Hz). But nav2's ObservationBuffer applies min_obstacle_height / max_obstacle_height in the costmap's OWN global frame, and the two costmaps do not share one. TF measured: odom->base_link z=+0.700, odom->base_scan z=+0.300, map->odom z=-0.700 (slam_toolbox flattens base_link to z=0 in map), map->base_scan z=-0.400. Both costmaps ship min_obstacle_height: 0.0 - so in `odom` the returns are at +0.30 m and are kept, and in `map` they are at -0.40 m and every one is discarded before it can mark.

caveat: Two attribution limits, stated so the numbers are not over-read. (1) `openral_sim.backends.robocasa.synthesize_laser_scan_2d` re-casts through the robot's own MuJoCo kinematic tree, so a self-return never enters /scan in sim in the first place. A clean silhouette here is the END STATE being correct; it is not proof that payload_scan_filter_node is what made it so. That attribution is what the deterministic sweep in tests/integration/test_nav2_scan_filter_live.py exists for - it ships a control that fails. (2) attached_objects stayed 0 on both runs (no policy was dispatched, so nothing was ever grasped), so the PAYLOAD half of the silhouette is unmeasured and is reported as payload_silhouette_measured: false rather than as a clean verdict.

self_mark_permanence: Separate finding, from making the live-lane sweep deterministic after it failed in CI. A self-return that reaches the cost grid ONCE is permanent. The scan filter fails open by design (a scan it cannot place is republished untouched - the more-obstacles direction), but it then removes exactly the beam whose ray would have cleared the cell it let through. Measured on a real nav2_costmap_2d with this package's topic wiring: phase 1, unfiltered ring at 0.20 m -> 32 cells marked inside the chassis; phase 2, filtered ring with every self beam = inf, 20 s -> still 32; phase 3, real returns at 3.0 m on the same bearings -> 0. Phase 3 is the control: Nav2's clearing works, there simply has to BE a ray. collision_monitor reads the same topic and has no costmap-side clearing at all. The obvious fix (write range_max instead of inf so the beam raytrace-clears) is NOT obviously safe - it turns the filter from 'leave the map alone' into 'erase 3 m along this bearing', so a beam dropped in error would delete a real obstacle. Recorded, not changed.

reproduction: Both scenes re-run in an independent session before merge, whole graph relaunched per scene. The conclusion reproduces and the incidental counts do not, which is what a live scene run looks like: local costmap ZERO LETHAL cells inside a 140 / 141-cell silhouette on baguette / deliver_straw, in samples carrying 127 / 59 marked cells elsewhere, base driven 0.954 / 1.318 m; global costmap max cost 0 on both, so the tool reports VACUOUS for the global half and exits non-zero. The two records that follow are that run's raw output. Recorded because this corpus's standing caveat is that its only two completions were never reproduced.
